Below is the letter from Nordstaff (we haven’t answered them anything, only from CS that it was forwarded to the relevant departments):

”Tere päevast

 

Palun uuesti edastada seda täiendatud kirja Courier Ops-ile ja juristile. 

Sain info Teie käes, et hetkel pole võimalik midagi teha, kuna Teie ei saa PPA kaudu jälgida, kas isik on vormistatud Eestis või mitte, kuigi see on Teie kohustus Välismaalaste seaduse järgi. 

Eestis on lubatud töötada Eesti kodanikul, isikul kellel on lühiajaline või pikaajaline elamisluba. Samuti EL kodanikul, kes on registreerinud ennast residentina Maksu- ja Tolliametis ja saanud PPA-s isikukoodi. 

Meie ettevõtte puhul tegemist on kolmanda riigi isikuga, kes ei ole lubatud Eestis töötada ja viibida ilma selleks ettenähtud seadusliku alust. Kolmanda riigi isikute puhul peab tööandja sama sissesõidu luba (ehk tööluba) PPA-s, et isikule on lubatud Eestis viibida ja töötada (*Välismaalaste seaduse § 104 lg 1).* Vormistamise ajal kontrollitakse kandidaati SIS süsteemis _(Schengeni infosüsteemis üksikisiku kohta säilitatav teave hõlmab järgmist: väljaandmistaotlused, teatud territooriumil viibimise ebasoovitavus, alaealisus, vaimuhaigus, kadunud inimese staatus, vajadus kaitse järele, taotlused õigusasutuse poolt ja kahtlustus kuriteos. Lisaks sisaldab süsteem andmeid kadunud, varastatud ja ebaseaduslikult omastatud tulirelvade, isikut tõendavate dokumentide, mootorsõidukite ja rahatähtede kohta.)_ ja peale seda tööandjale väljastatakse lühiajalise töötamise registreerimise.

Lühiajalise töötamise saab registreerida kuni 365 päevaks 455-päevase perioodi jooksul või hooajalise töö puhul 270 päevaks 365-päevase perioodi jooksul. _Erand on saanud ajutise kaitse isikud, kes ei vaja tööluba või isikud, kes olid EL-s enne sõja algust ja nende viibimise alus on automaatselt pikentatud hädaolukorra lõpuni (allikas 1.07.2022 määrus)._ 

Nordstaff OÜ-l kehtib kutsuja kohustus ehk ta peab garanteerima isikule kaitset, õigeaegselt sätestatud töötasu kättesaamist, majutust jaa nii edasi (*VMS § 290 lg-dele 1 kuni 3, 1, § 106 lg 1, § 18 lg 1*).

*Bolt Operation OÜ* poole pöördub kolmanda riigi isik ja soovib töötada kullerina. Enne tööle asumist ta peab Teile tõestama, et tal on õigus töötada Eestis ja selleks ta peab esitama registreerimise ajal enda tööluba ja kirjaliku nõusoleku juhatuse liige poolt koos pitsiga, et tööandja lubab registreerida töötamise samaaegselt ka teises ettevõttes. Nõusoleku peal peab olema märgitud kontakt, et Bolt saaks ühendust võtta ja kontrollida, kas tegemist ei ole võltsinguga. 

Teine asi, mida peab tegema Bolt Operations OÜ, kontrollima, kas isik on tõesti registreeritud PPA-s ([https://www.politsei.ee/et/paringud/luehiajalise-eestis-toeoetamise-registreerimise-kontroll|https://www.politsei.ee/et/paringud/luehiajalise-eestis-toeoetamise-registreerimise-kontroll|smart-link] ) (*VMS § 286 lg 1 ja 1.1*). Kuna tööluba võib olla ka võltsitud, et saada Eestis tööd ja isikul on ammu ületatud biomeetriline viibimine. 

Vahest on ka olukordi, kus isik lõpetab lepingu enda kutsuja ettevõttes (*VMS § 52 lg 9)*, ja arvab, et saab ka edasi viibida ja töötada Eestis ilma ümbervosrmistamiseta, kuigi see ei ole nii *(VMS § 80*). Välismaalase viisa ja tööluba automaatselt tühistatakse *(VMS § 109 lg 1,* *§ 78 lg 9, § 73).* Uus tööandja peab vormistama talle viibimise alust nii kiiresti kui võimalik ka selleks, et vormistatud viisa jääks kehtivaks. 

Kuna Nordstaff Oܠja Bolt Operations Oܠvahel ei ole sõlmitud koostöölepingut, siis meie töölubadega isikud ei saa töötada Teie juures. Bolt Operations Oܠpeab taotlema antud isikule PPA-s lühiajalist töötamist, ja registreerima neid vastavalt seadusele. Oleme teadlikud, et Bolt ei ole otsene tööandja kulleritele, kuigi teenust ei või osutada isik, kellel puudub selleks ette nähtud seaduslik alus. Kolmanda riigi isik saab avada FIE või Oܠainult e-residentsuse abil, teistel juhtudel ta peab olema vormistatud Bolt Operations Oܠtöötajana. 

Näidisena toon välja meie töötaja Pavel Samsi (isikukood 39809040085), kes töötab Teie juures kullerina Pärnu linnas. Registreerimise ajal ta oli Teile näidanud meie tööluba, lisasin seda manusena ning selle järgi sai liigipääsu Teie süsteemile. Kuigi ta poole esitanud meie nõusoleku ehk tähendab see seda, et Bolt Operation Oܠon võtnud kolmanda isiku tööle ilma vastavat registreerimist. Ja vastavalt *VMS § 301 lg-dele 1 ja 2*, tööandja poolt välismaalase Eestis töötamise tingimuste rikkumise võimaldamise eest, sealhulgas välismaalase poolt seadusliku alusega kindlaks määratud tingimustele mittevastava töötamise võimaldamise eest karistatakse rahatrahviga kuni 300 trahviühikut. Sama teo eest, kui selle on toime pannud juriidiline isik karistatakse rahatrahviga kuni 32 000 eurot. Meie teada, Pavlile pole vormistatud ega taotletud lühiajalist töötamist teine ettevõtte, ja tema ei ole e-resident. 

Pavli puhul veel märgin seda, et tema LTR on registreeritud kuni 05.04.2023 aasta, kuigi tema viibimis alus lõpeb 07.02.2023 (saab täis periood 365 päeva) ning peale nimetatud tähtaega Teie ei saa teda vormistada tööle. Peale 07.02.2023 kui ta ei lahku Eestis ta saab illegaaliks *(VMS* *§ 43 lg 3, § 44 lg 1, § 54 lg 2, § 55, § 78 lg 9, § 80).*

Näidena toon välja seda, et näiteks, patrullpolitsei peatub Pavli riikumise tõttu tööajal kullerina ja teeb passi kontrolli. Selgub, et antud isikul on Moldova pass, siis politsei teeb päringu PPA-sse, kus tema tööandjaks on Nordstaff OÜ. 

Eestis kehtib solidaarne vastutus. Süsteemis nad näevad, et puudub info Bolt Operation Oܠkohta ja tööluba, samuti puudub süsteemis meievaheline koostööleping. Pavel saab ettekirjutuse ja depoortimise kuni 10 aastat. Bolt Operation OÜ-le väljastatakse rahatrahvi kuni 32 000 eurot ja tehakse märge ebaseadusliku vormistamise kohta *(VMS § 104 lg 2*), samuti kohustatakse maksma kogu välismaalasele maksmata jäänud töötasu, sealhulgas töötasust kinnipeetavad seaduses ettenähtud maksud ja maksed *(VMS § 286 lg 1)*. Bolt Operation Oܠpuhul see rikkub mainet ja mõjutab PPA usaldusväärsuse hinnangut tulevikus (*VMS § 40 lg-dele 3 ja 4, § 296 lg 1).* 

Kuna Bolt Operations Oܠei ole vormistanud töölubasid siis vastavalt *VMS* *§ 300 lg 2* juriidilist isikut karistatakse rahatrahviga kuni 32 000 eurot. Mainime ka seda, et kui tööle oli võetud kolmanda riigi isik, Bolt Operations OÜ-l on kohustatud säilitama välismaalase töötamise ajal ja kümme aastat pärast välismaalase töötamise lõpetamist koopiaid andmetest ja dokumentidest, mis tõendavad välismaalase Eestis töötamise õigusliku aluse olemasolu tema töölevõtmisel ja töötamise ajal *(VMS § 286 lg 4).*

*Kuna Nordstaff Oܠpoole annud enda nõusoleku ja puudub teiepoolne vastav PPA taotlus, siis antud isik ei saa töötada kullerina.* Palume ka tulevikus mitte registreerida uusi inimesi meie töölubaga Teie süsteemis, meievahel puudub koostööleping ning Bolt Operations Oܠei ole kasutajaettevõte. Kuna Pavel oli ainult üks näide, siis peale Teie vastust saadame veel nimekirja, kes töötab Teie juures ebaseaduslikult. 

 

Palun saata mulle kirjaliku vastuse, et Courier team on seda kirja kätte saanud ja seda olukorda lahendatakse. 

Lisaküsimuste korral, meeleldi vastan.

    COUNT(DISTINCT co.user_id) total_users,
    count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment IS true THEN co.order_id end) as fail_orders,
    round(SUM (CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment IS true THEN co.capture_amount_total end),0) as GMV_fail,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment IS true THEN co.user_id end) fail_users,
    CASE WHEN all_orders>0 THEN ROUND(((1.0*fail_orders)/(1.0*all_orders)),2) END as orders_ratio,
    CASE WHEN gmv_total >0 THEN ROUND(((1.0*GMV_fail)/(1.0*gmv_total)),2) END as GMV_ratio,
    CASE WHEN total_users >0 THEN ROUND(((1.0*fail_users)/(1.0*total_users)),2) END as users_ratio,
    round(avg (CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment IS true THEN co.capture_amount_total end),1) as AVG_fail_order,
    round(avg (ffc.prediction),1) as AVG_ML,
    count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.is_initial_failed_payment IS true THEN co.order_id end) as fail_INITIAL_orders,
    round(SUM (CASE WHEN co.is_initial_failed_payment IS true THEN co.capture_amount_total end),0) as GMV_INITIAL_fail,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.is_initial_failed_payment IS true THEN co.user_id end) fail_INITIAL_users,
    CASE WHEN all_orders>0 THEN ROUND(((1.0*fail_INITIAL_orders)/(1.0*all_orders)),2) END as orders_INITIAL_ratio,
    CASE WHEN gmv_total >0 THEN ROUND(((1.0*GMV_INITIAL_fail)/(1.0*gmv_total)),2) END as GMV_INITIAL_ratio,
    CASE WHEN total_users >0 THEN ROUND(((1.0*fail_INITIAL_users)/(1.0*total_users)),2) END as users_INITIAL_ratio

order by users_ratio desc

Hey team,

Here to put my 2 cents. So, for B4B clients, we usually issue an invoice for each ride. When a company moves to resale model mid-month, we also issue a monthly invoice at the end of the month, which includes those previously individually charged rides. Therefore it looks like we issue double invoices. This is why we always discourage mid-month changes. Such changes should be done in a way that would be effective starting from the new invoicing period (1st of each month in most cases).

So, I suppose the issue is rather global than PL specific. However, if I understand correctly from [~accountid:62b9a75a37780d89a3507d57]'s words, in PL clients need to declare both invoices - which might create questions for tax authorities about Bolt as it looks like double income. In addition, some companies might possibly use it as a mean to launder money.

For the specific case, unfortunately there is no way to change the invoices for this client. However, I escalated the overall issue to the product team and it is currently being discussed. Possible approach we will take is likely to block mid-month changes so this won’t happen again.

This driver is accepting rides and not going towards the pickup locations, then cancels the rides after marking as arrived - examples ([1|https://ghana-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1205301011/1325751169],[2|https://ghana-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1205310254/1325761533],[3|https://ghana-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1205317964/1325769691])

We automatically block if they have many of such rides because:

* We preauthorise the ride price from the rider’s card to secure the payment and avoid failed payments/fraud, and when the ride is cancelled, sometimes it may take a day or two for the bank to release this money and this causes tickets to CS and overall inconvenience.
* The rider gets a notification that the driver accepted the ride, but then nothing happens, and we don’t automatically match them with a new driver when the ride is cancelled, so they need to go through the order steps again to place a new one, and in addition they might get a different price compared to the cancelled ride.

This can create a very bad user experience for our riders.

If the driver doesn’t want to do the ride, then they should reject it when they first receive the offer, and not right after they accept it.

I’ve removed the block as this driver has quite many rides and good ratings. It is also very good that the driver was educated about this.

Best,

Francesca

* Inform the driver lead that the application was deleted as per their request.

UPD {{2022-08-29}} - summary of the project kick-off call (organised by prod and eng teams, EP was participating too)

* Relocation process, additional notes:
** FleetB initiates the request for driver relocation. They go through the usual flow of inviting a driver.
** Driver gets the link to join the fleetB. Our system automatically identifies if the driver has an active account or not. If they have, they are asked to log in and then confirm the transition to a new fleet. If not, they are going through the current driver registration flow.
*** The current issue - it is not clear how to identify the current driver. The eng team will split the task into two and take the driver identification issue separately. No ETA, most likely we will not be involved.
** FleetA gets a notification via email to confirm or reject the driver relocation to a new fleet. If fleetA rejects, the relocation process is stopped. If fleetA confirms or does not reply within 7 days, our system proceeds with the driver relocation.
** Driver gets notifications if their relocation is confirmed or rejected. If the relocation is completed, they get notifications regarding this and a link to log in (it should and most likely will happen like this). If the driver relocation is rejected, the driver gets the notification but without the rejection reason.
*** If the driver relocation is not possible to be completed automatically (see [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Dnha2RYcVLO_nIAX2wcqH2vMtIOYGTvAXKkTfM0rff8/edit#|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Dnha2RYcVLO_nIAX2wcqH2vMtIOYGTvAXKkTfM0rff8/edit#|smart-link] for more details), then they get a notification that they should contact us for the transition to be done. _Most probably CS will escalate those cases to the local OPS teams._
* Before the relocation but after confirmation from the driver, the driver can use their previous account.
* If the relocation happens before the payout, the driver gets a notification about their pending balance and that the payout from fleetA should be transferred by the EOW or within usual timeline.
* *No precise ETA for the feature release*. Issues with driver identification should be solved first.

After discussion with [~accountid:5c575a2cbe86ba3abff04cad] I’ve found out:

* The peek number of online drivers is about 100k: [grafana stats|http://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/000000014/drivers-orders?orgId=1&refresh=30m&viewPanel=19&from=now-24h&to=now&var-country=All&var-city=All&var-driver_state=All&var-order_state=All&var-shard_id=All]
* This means that MQTT broker has to handle 100k MQTT clients/connections
* Each app makes call to the server once in 2 seconds, so we have ~50k requests per second 
* Requests are served 2 purposes: determine driver location, fetch current state (for instance: notifications)
* To minimize latency and restrict damage we need a broker per shard
* We need to provide solution with ability to scale to handle x10 more drivers/requests
* Take into account rider polling load. It is harder to estimate as rider app doesn't poll in the background, but we can say that it is should be in the ballpark of the number of people actively searching: [grafana stats|http://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/qyeV4yAMz/customers-demand-monitoring?orgId=1&viewPanel=4]

After having spoken to our advisor, we have been informed that there is no specific guidance on tips in SK, and as long as the tips are given voluntarily and clearly being added after delivery fees, then any tips should be outside the scope of VAT - so we do not have to add VAT on the tips.

However, since there is no specific guidance or legislation on the topic this conclusion might change either through legislation or if the tax agency starts a tax audit. We need to bear in mind that we are issuing the delivery fee invoices on behalf of couriers, and the VAT reporting and payment obligation lies with them as well. When we say “No VAT to be added” we are saying that invoices issued by couriers do not need to have VAT added on the line for tips. 

This is how it looks in most of the EU as a starting point, but countries do differ so doing a per-country review is still a good idea.

# Changing the error text on the *backend*. It is considered impossible since it is a rate limiter message and rate limiter is a part of Framework and not customisable

# Overriding the error message on the *client*.
# Introduce throttling for this button on the *client*.

Since both backend solutions are considered as impossible or insecure, this bug could be fixed only on the client side.

We have now received feedback from our PT tax advisors, which is as follows: 

* A customer’s NIF (B2C) must be included on the invoice upon their request.
* In cases where the customer (B2C) requests for the inclusion of their NIF subsequent to the issuing of the original invoice, the correct procedure to be adopted is to issue a credit note mentioning the original invoice and then issue a new invoice including the customer’s NIF. Please note that the Portuguese law does not establish a time limit for the customer to request the reissue of the invoice. However, since the Portuguese VAT Code establish a maximum of a 2 years period to correct invoice errors in case of over assessed VAT (article 78(3) of the Portuguese VAT Code), the same time limit should apply to cases where the customer requests for the inclusion of their NIF on the invoice.
* There should be no negative (tax) consequences resulting from the inclusion of the customer’s NIF on all invoices if we decided to go this direction. Thus, if we collected and included the customer’s NIF upon registration on the platform and always included such info on the invoice, then this would be OK from a PT tax law perspective.

SQL used for analysis:

{code:sql}SELECT
country,
card_country,
DATE_TRUNC('month',created) AS MONTH,
COUNT(CASE WHEN fraud=TRUE THEN order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_orders,
COUNT(order_id) AS count_of_orders,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN fraud=1 THEN user_price_eur ELSE 0 END),0) AS sum_of_fraud_orders,
ROUND(SUM(user_price_eur),0) AS sum_of_orders,
ROUND(count_of_fraud_orders*100.0/count_of_orders,1) AS fraud_count_ratio,
ROUND(sum_of_fraud_orders*100.0/sum_of_orders,1) AS fraud_count_ratio
FROM (
	SELECT DISTINCT
	etl.country_code AS country,
	etl.order_id,
	etl.user_price,
	etl.user_price/r.rate AS user_price_eur,
	etl.created,
	rd.payment_method_type,
	rd.card_country AS card_country,
	--CASE WHEN rd.card_country<>etl.country_code THEN 'foreign' ELSE 'local' END AS foreign_card,
	rd.card_age_in_days AS card_age,
	rd.user_device_created_age_in_days AS device_age,
	CASE WHEN etl.is_payment_problem=TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_payment_problem,
	CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback=TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_chargeback,
	CASE WHEN etl.payment_collection_status='accept_any' THEN etl.uncovered_amount ELSE 0 END AS uncovered_amount,
	CASE WHEN etl.payment_collection_status='accept_any' THEN etl.uncovered_amount/r.rate ELSE 0 END AS uncovered_amount_eur,
	CASE WHEN etl.fraud_label=TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS fraud
	FROM etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
	LEFT JOIN pii.etl_archive_analytical_delivery_order_request_data AS rd ON rd.id=etl.fraud_calculation_id
	LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON etl.price_currency = r.currency AND date_trunc('day', etl.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on)
	WHERE order_type='food_delivery'
	AND etl.created BETWEEN '2022-05-01' AND '2022-09-01'
	AND etl.country_code='gh'
	AND rd.payment_method_type='adyen'
	AND rd.card_country<>etl.country_code
	AND etl.order_state='finished'
	AND ((rd.card_country='us' AND etl.user_price>=90 AND rd.card_age_in_days<15)
		OR (rd.card_country='br' AND rd.card_age_in_days<45))
)
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY 1,2,3{code}

UPD {{2022-08-30}} 

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1n3PhP1Dw5e8d6dZyEhNYLrDgM1xc0mONQSBkRdYcMb4/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1n3PhP1Dw5e8d6dZyEhNYLrDgM1xc0mONQSBkRdYcMb4/edit#gid=0|smart-link](_SD tickets created May-June 22_ tab)

* Based on the nr of tickets received in May - June 2022, we can go with one request type for processes and one for self-help.
* The request type for _Other questions_ seems to be abused, potentially due to the fewer fields to be filled in.
* Other request types for launches, typos, and updates seem like doing fine and fulfilling its purpose.

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1n3PhP1Dw5e8d6dZyEhNYLrDgM1xc0mONQSBkRdYcMb4/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1n3PhP1Dw5e8d6dZyEhNYLrDgM1xc0mONQSBkRdYcMb4/edit#gid=0|smart-link](_Form Responses 1_ & _Responses - categorised_ tabs)

*Note*: There were no answers from the Content Leads working with Bolt Food and Bolt Market.

* On a scale from 1 to 10, the subjective quality of the SD tickets received is rated as 7 (average). It looks like it can be improved.
* Based on answers, it seems that the quality of the requests can differ based on the business line (they are overall better for Bolt Drive) and regions (they are overall worse for UK).
** Thus, seems like we don’t need a lot of changes, but a few - to unify the request type layouts for all the request types, especially for _other questions and ideas_.
* The proposed layouts were described as long - this was actioned, some of the fields indeed could have been merged to make it easier to fill in the form and then work with the request.
* The information (fields) mentioned as needed from the beginning:
** clear explanation of the issue - 100% of respondents
** link to the article - 80%
** POC or other stakeholders - 60%
** referred documents + access to them + context - 40%
** clear request description - 40%
** reason for requesting an improvement + impact - 40%
** ticket example - 40%
** is there a process or not - 20%

*To sum up:*

* We can go with one request type per _concrete product/outcome of our team’s work_: one for trainings, one for self-help, one for processes, one for MKA (to be added for the Quality team). Request types for launches, updates, and typos will not be changed.
* The request type for _other questions and ideas_ will be modified not to be used for all types of requests and be more for questions that are indeed not relevant to any of the well-defined request types.
* The subjective quality of the SD tickets received is rated as 7. After the changes are introduced, in a month or 2 months, it will make sense to ask Content Leads to rate the quality of the SD tickets received again to measure the impact of the changes.
* The most needed information for Content Leads to work on requests is clear explanation of the issue, link to the relevant article, POC or other stakeholders to be included, clear request description, clear description of the reason, ticket examples, and relevant documents. These should be covered in the request type layout.

Posting here what I have just shared with Laima and Krzysztof: 

Last year, [@Kasia|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UKE25J2KF] announced [this|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CM30FTRHP/p1614676653038300] for the UK market, and I understand that this initiative came directly from Nick Smith due to the cost of outgoing contact.

For a long time, we have not included in any process to send a message when we provide a refund to drivers. There has been no change to the process itself which has caused this recent increase in driver confusion. The move to Beehive also should not have triggered this.

So where this sudden increase in driver confusion has come from, I’m not sure. The only other thing that has changed in terms of refunds is, I believe, selecting the driver as the refund actor. I think the CS Product team pushed this change, but would need to check. (It also happened quite a while ago).

*CS sending outbound messages will not completely solve the issue* due to some automations that also affect the driver balance. This is why the information should be clear to drivers in the app, however, currently it is not.

I also agree it’s bad customer service, but I don't think that the _long-term_ solution here is for CS to take on this task or the cost of contacting drivers. I can add a temporary update to this process for us to send outgoing messages only if Nick says yes to this.

My perspective is that we should push for a product solution here. It doesn’t only confuse drivers in the UK market, and at the end of the day, the drivers should be able to understand what’s happening with their balance using the app and not have to rely on CS contact. 

Having CS manually send outgoing messages to drivers opens a channel between the driver and CS that doesn’t otherwise exist, and ultimately increases CS cost.

*Delivery (highest impact to lowest & in the past 3 months)*

* Cyprus 🇨🇾  - Courier ~4k EUR:
** They have a campaign running in August where they adjusting 20 EUR multiple times per week but should end in September:
*** +€20 for every Courier that completes at least 15 deliveries within a day (08:00 - 23:00)
*** We offer €20 bonus to couriers that go online and stay online from 8:00-12:00am and have acceptance rate of 90%
** No issues with duplicates (as the market isn’t actually that large which we can’t keep track of the files)
* Malta 🇲🇹  - Courier ~3k EUR:
** Local team is using dummy courier profiles linked to the fleet to sell bags in bulk. Tracking happens locally via Google Sheets 
** They also have a charity initiative & couriers are partnering with Food Banks to provide food for those who need it the most. This process is currently under review (so we all know what this means) - non-existent. Good initiative tho
** No issues with duplicates (keeping track pretty good as the market isn’t that large)
* Ukraine 🇺🇦 - Courier ~1.2k EUR:
** Large inner migration due to war & partners with multiple courier accounts (1 per city) were affected. Bags were returned / given out to the same partner (but several courier profiles) hence the same person & the same bag was charged multiple times. These were backtracked & adjusted manually later + couriers reached out about their balance later as well. 
** They are tracking duplicates locally in Google sheets (via order ID & order ref.) but automatic duplicate detection would be nice to have. Also beneficial for providers as they’re running 5-10 adjustments per week - would have to check duplicates across several files for the same week
* Poland 🇵🇱 - Courier / Provider ~1k EUR: 
** Courier:
*** They too are using these dummy courier accounts to adjust fleet’s balance e.g. sign up 20 couriers you’ll get 2000 pln etc
*** Running several campaigns e.g. for churned couriers, couriers that registered but never delivered and performance bonus for making 75 orders. The same courier completed multiple campaigns hence the adjustments were run multiple times (although no differentiation between the campaigns in the backend)
** Provider (~300 EUR): 
*** Definitely some issues with adjustments as CS are adding these to the sheet & local OPS are not able to verify the sheet as the market is pretty large & those sheets are quite large. The impact isn’t huge but showing duplicates in Admin could help the local OPS for sure
*** And some providers like to buy the photos we make & some of them need these to be photographed several times over a period hence the adjustments are run after it’s finalised
* Estonia 🇪🇪 - Provider ~1k EUR:
** Providers have multiple tablets & fees under one account → hence the duplicate adjustments but these are edge cases
** Actual duplicate tablet rent/fee adjustments are happening as local team are not able to confirm the entries on the adjustment sheet.

*Conclusion*

In general local team definitely are trying their best to avoid the duplicate adjustments & from the feedback 80% of the cases the duplicate adjustment is correct. Which gives us realistic impact of 800 eur per month (~10k EUR annually / 0.002% GMV) globally due to duplicate manual adjustments

Task to be resumed during September according to AZ team’s request.

*Rides (highest impact to lowest & in the past 3 months)*

* UK 🇬🇧 - Driver ~12k EUR:
** Majority is from the launched cities (e.g. Manchester) with driver-to-rider bonus. Local ops are keeping track of this on their own & as the volumes aren’t too large they can manage it . Capped at 100 GBP per week & ended on 5th August
*** £10 bonus for every time a ‘new’ rider uses his/her code. The rider gets £5 off their first trip.
** Compensations - CS doesn’t check for any duplicates hence 100% sure invalid & duplicate adjustments are happening. Each and every compensation issued by CS goes to [this sheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DXeyMO9iTWGeJBqYeNFiSCeZGvuNLwYMB8PIsgkzmc0/].
** Impact ~400 EUR for 3 months / 1600 EUR annually
* Spain 🇪🇸  - Driver ~6.5k EUR:
** 30% of rides in Spain are cash orders. Which means if a rider cancels, drivers reach out to CS and request cancellation fee to be compensated for their time and efforts. There is a Beehive automation that automatically compensates them 3 times per week for the cash CF (so no ticket to CS is created). If the driver reaches out due to this same issue more than 3 per week, a ticket is created with CS. CS will then confirm if the request is valid (did he go to the pick up location, did he wait there etc) & add it to [this sheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1x6x_sRT_i-jStWp4EgWmFp0lo5aZ9O5MQrPff91dm18/edit#gid=349592768] as a separate line. The CSV will automatically flag the duplicate entries (every market should use this ^^ as a template)
** No issues with duplicates
* Germany 🇩🇪  - Driver ~6k EUR:
** There is a Berlin Driver League (for 8 weeks) going on, where top 10 drivers who receives Bonuses, in the beginning of a new week. Since there is some manual work that goes into deciding upon the weekly winners, they have to manually compensate them. Record [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18qCXkRIOC4eVJXHxRx6agT7uyqLC9tFpIeLtN-HaThE/edit#gid=0]. I love this.
** No issues with duplicates
* Romania 🇷🇴  - Driver / Fleet ~5k EUR:
** Driver ~2k EUR:
*** Using dummy accounts to compensate the company mainly for branding but also airport booking fees. In Brasov, where we have a few cars paid lower than the normal scheme, for more rides (but this one is monthly). 
** Fleet ~3k EUR:
*** Lead by compensations for branding. Weekly bonuses (e.g. 200 each per driver) for drivers who manage to complete a number of rides, varies between 30 and 70, depending on how the city is performing. Also are paying to the FOs directly because some of the branded cars are owned by the FO & it’s cheaper for us this way
** They keep all their compensations details in [this file|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZE9LmeGWOdVPudjhBkbqA9RLAUl74Av_wgqH-4axgdw/edit#gid=1536597627]. & no issues with duplicate entries
* Croatia 🇭🇷 - Driver ~3k EUR:
** Running adjustments for branding bonus. Drivers own multiple vehicles hence during the same week the same compensation is given multiple times. They have tiers for the amounts e.g. finished 400 rides, getting 1000 HRK. Technically they can put only one driver ID with sum of branding bonuses but currently for them this is easier way to track branding program because as mentioned above, one driver can be in charged for several branded cars.
** No issues with duplicate entries. 

*Conclusion*

Although there is a lot of entries in the sheets which show up as duplicates most of them are verified & tracked by the local team. Of course there is some edge cases where the adjustment row is added twice but the impact is negligible (more likely to be happen due to connection issues vs double escalation from the driver). As I’ve checked the top 5 countries the impact is ~6% of the initially estimated value. This comes to 800 EUR per month / ~10k EUR annually (same as Delivery) / 0.0003% of GMV hence neglible.

Article 39 describes the tasks of the DPO. Based on Article 39 (1) lit. d she/he shall cooperate with the supervisory authority. Recitals do not elaborate on this cooperation obligation in further detail.

h3. *Guidelines of the Art-29-Working Group*

Nevertheless the Guidelines of the Art-29-Working Group ([https://ec.europa.eu/newsroom/article29/items/612048/en|https://ec.europa.eu/newsroom/article29/items/612048/en|smart-link] ) give a better insight on how rDPAs view this obligation.:
_”_*_4.3. Cooperating with the supervisory authority and acting as a contact point_*
_According to Article 39(1)(d) and (e), the DPO should ‘cooperate with the supervisory authority’ and ‘act as a contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing, including the prior consultation referred to in Article 36, and to consult, where appropriate, with regard to any other matter’._
_These tasks refer to the_ *_role of ‘facilitator’ of the DPO mentioned in the introduction to these Guidelines._* _The DPO acts as a contact point to facilitate_ *_access by the supervisory authority to the documents and information for the performance of the tasks mentioned in Article 57_*_, as well as for the_ *_exercise of its investigative, corrective, authorisation, and advisory powers mentioned in Article 58_*_. As already mentioned, the DPO is bound by secrecy or confidentiality concerning the performance of his or her tasks, in accordance with Union or Member State law (Article 38(5)). However, the obligation of secrecy/confidentiality does not prohibit the DPO from contacting and seeking advice from the supervisory authority. Article 39(1)(e) provides that the DPO can consult the supervisory authority on any other matter, where appropriate.”_

*Authorities like CNIL provide the following guidance (*[*https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/atoms/files/guide_pratique_rgpd_-_delegues_a_la_protection_des_donnees.pdf*|https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/atoms/files/guide_pratique_rgpd_-_delegues_a_la_protection_des_donnees.pdf]*)*

The DPO is, on the one hand, required to cooperate with the supervisory authority and, as such, must play the role of “facilitator” during exchanges with the CNIL (response to requests during an on-site inspection, investigation of a complaint, consultation within the framework of a DPIA, notification of a data breach, etc.).
In addition, the DPO may consult the CNIL on all matters relating to the protection of personal data or his function. The data controller or the data processor is prohibited from submitting these questions to its validation or from prohibiting them. In addition, according to the Charter of support for professionals that it published in February 2021, the CNIL does not respond to requests for advice sent to it by organizations that have not taken the trouble to consult their DPO on the question they wish to ask.

The majority of CNIL on-site inspections are unannounced. However, in exceptional cases, the *organization and the DPO* may be notified a few days in advance. The DPO may, during an on-site inspection, be *“responsible for the premises”* where the processing operation(s) that are the subject of the checks are located. In this case, the DPO is the privileged, but not exclusive, interlocutor of the inspection delegation and is responsible for reviewing and signing the report drawn up at the end of the day. The data controller remains able to comment on the report when it is sent to him. On the other hand, the *DPO may not represent the organization alone before the CNIL* during a summonsed hearing, as this would *put him in a conflict of interest situation*. He can however accompany a representative of the organization to bring his expertise and answer questions. 

What does the appointment of a DPO bring if my organization already has a legal department competent in matters of data protection?A legal team, even a competent one, cannot replace the advantages of appointing a DPO:

* it is a point of contact that can be easily found and reached, both internally and externally;
* he combines legal and IT security knowledge;
* his independence, defined by a legal text, ensures his impartiality and the freedom of his recommendations;
* He can benefit from support and assistance from the CNIL.

h3. *Additional remarks*

It is the task of the DPO to *cooperate with the supervisory authority* and to act as a *contact point for the supervisory authority* on issues related to the processing, including prior consultation pursuant to Art. 36 and, where appropriate, to provide advice on all other issues. This is intended to *facilitate the work of the supervisory authority.* The DPO acts as a central point of contact for supervisory authorities because he knows internal processing and organizational processes and is in theory an understanding contact person due to his specialist knowledge.The DPO is also to be named in the list of processing activities, which is to be handed over to the supervisory authority on request. Likewise, the notification of violations of the protection of personal data to the supervisory authority according to Art. 33 must contain the contact details of the DPO. 

The DPO can also play a more extensive role in this reporting obligation, but their duty of loyalty as an employee must also be taken into account here, so that they must first exhaust all internal options before contacting the supervisory authority. It is doubtful that contact with the supervisory authority can subsequently be restricted in view of the obligation to cooperate (especially if the contact originates from the supervisory authority) and the right to consult the supervisory authority for advice. 

h3. Recommendation (oDPO)

If Privacy Team is stating that the oDPO should take of AKI-letters and collecting the necessary input, we could reach out to the business and ask for the necessary information *(However, this would conflict with PrivacyTeams's request to approach the business via the Privacy Team to avoid confusion).*  oDPO could collect information and copy and paste the input of the business without any regards to the interests of the company when editing *(the data protection officer only takes care of the protection of the rights and freedoms of the data subjects and the implementation of the GDPR)*. 

Furthermore, a final approval of the company's statement by the DPO is not possible, since the DPO has purely advisory powers and is not allowed to make any decisions. In this respect, a responsible body in the company (CEO, Head of Leagal or Head of Privacy) must approve the statement. Whoever that should be. 


*The oDPO could receive the letters, reach out to the business to get the necessary information and sent the information collected to the supervisory authority (if the controller has given its approval). Due to a lack of knowledge of Estonian language, due to the fact that when compiling the results, the oDPO is not allowed to adapt any unfavorable formulations in favour/ in the interest of the controller and also due to the fact that the DPO is not allowed to sign/approve the controller's statement however, it is recommended that the privacy team remains involved in the process as the in privacy matters knowledgeable department of the controller.*

Also just keep in mind, if Bolt does not comply with orders of the DPA, the controller is facing a fine (Checkin *§§ 69, 70 of the Estonian Privacy Act)*[https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/104012019011|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/104012019011|smart-link] )*.*

*§ 69.* *Failure to comply with the order of the Data Protection Inspectorate*
 (1) Failure to comply with the order stipulated in Article 58(2) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council -
shall be punished with a fine of up to 20,000,000 euros.
 (2) For the same act, if it is committed by a legal entity, -
shall be punished with a fine of up to 20,000,000 euros or up to 4 percent of its global annual turnover of the previous financial year, whichever is greater.

*§ 70. Violation of granting access to the Data Protection Inspectorate*
  (1) Failure to comply with an order issued on the basis of the investigative authority provided for in Article 58, paragraph 1 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if it does not allow the Data Protection Inspectorate access to personal data, other information or premises, -
shall be punished with a fine of up to 20,000,000 euros.
  (2) For the same act, if it is committed by a legal entity, -
shall be punished with a fine of up to 20,000,000 euros or up to 4 percent of its global annual turnover of the previous financial year, whichever is greater.

Here’s a recap:

*How attachments are handled now*

* we upload them with {{ACL: "public-read"}}, which makes public resources in the internet
* we upload them with fairly simple keys, so security is at even more risk
* we store the direct public S3 urls in support case events and ship them to the frontend
* when downloaded by the frontend, there isn’t any more meta-data about the file, so the browser uses the auto-generated S3 object key as the filename, which is different than the original filename
* since we have a direct S3 url, we can bypass the beehive auth and support case permission checks

During the grooming, there was a decision made to build a backend endpoint, which would:

* do auth checks
* verify support case permissions/access
* download the file from S3 and return it with a proper filename

However, this makes our backend a party in file transfers. Those files would either need to be loaded to memory, or to a temporary file on disk - I’m not sure if it’s possible to create an endpoint in NJSC which allows us to stream the response from a buffer from S3.
We could still prevent adding this additional load of file transfers from our backend.

*What I would like to propose short term*

* we upload the attachments with {{ACL: "private"}}, so that only the owner can access them, the files are no longer public in the internet
* S3 object keys can stay the same, since they are either way not accessible publicly
* we upload the attachments with an additional parameter: {{ContentDisposition: attachment; filename="<original filename>"}} , which is a standard http directive for telling the browser what should be the filename of the attachment saved
* we don’t store the direct public S3 urls in support case events, instead we generate signed urls to the attachments the moment the case messages for agent are requested
* generated signed url has its expiry time, it will stop working after a configured amount of time
* when downloaded by the frontend, there is metadata about the file, so the browser uses the filename provided
* since we don’t have a direct public S3 url, instead just a temporary signed url, lack of auth and permission checks is not a problem - auth and permissions were verified when fetching case messages

The above will fix the filenames for the future attachments.
All the existing attachments will still be public and have wrong filenames when saved.

*What I would like to propose long term*

* Use the same {{ContentDisposition}} directive, but not during the upload, but rather when generating the signed url to get the S3 object, it’s applied the same way
* It is not possible now, because NJSC S3 interface does not allow it, we would need to add this feature to NJSC
* Since the content disposition is applied dynamically when fetching the case messages, even the old attachments will get the proper filename metadata when saved

After that, we would need to think of how to migrate old “public” attachments to “private” ones.

Nothing to test here - fully technical task.

*Incident summary*: driver trip sharing safety feature configuration had an issue where the rider's first name was exposed via the shared link to third parties. The feature foresees that driver can share the trip details (live location data) with friends and family. The feature design did not include sharing the rider’s first name, only the trip’s location data. The link stays active for up to 48 hours if a ride is not finished. Accessing a link after the ride is finished will notify the user that the link is expired.

*Timeframe:* The feature went live globally on 17.08.22, the issue was noticed day later on 18.08.22, and fixed (removing rider name) on 22.08.22.

*Scope*: the feature was rolled out globally; the estimation is currently not possible as we don’t have the backend events that could measure how many links were opened. 

*Decision on risk and notification*: disclosure of the first name (of the passenger (combined with the location data)) during the time of the ride had a low/medium risk and external notification is not required. Nevertheless there has to be actions to mitigate the risk in the future. 

*Corrective actions are taken/to be taken:* 

* Product review the QA process and will further improve on having a technical kickoff for every single feature to review the requirements, engage more with product council (Julius) and privacy council (Liis), PM’s take more active role to test features before launch.  
* Product will implement a possibility to explore in the backend events that could measure how many links were opened.

Query used:

{noformat}with base as 
(
	select ebdd.client_id, ic.external_id as driver_id, max("date") as last_balance_entry_date,
	sum((1 - paid_ratio)*amount_due/coalesce(vcer.rate, 1)) as unpaid_debt
	from etl_billing_debt_driver ebdd 
	left join invoicing_client ic on ic.id = ebdd.client_id 
	left join vw_currency_exchange_rates vcer on vcer.valid_on = date('2022-08-30') and vcer.currency = ebdd.currency 
	where ic."type" = 'Driver' and ic.country = 'ke'
	group by 1, 2
	having last_balance_entry_date between date('2021-08-01') and date('2022-04-01')
		and unpaid_debt > 0
)
select sum(unpaid_debt), count(distinct client_id)
--percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by unpaid_debt) as perc25_unpaid_debt,
--percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by unpaid_debt) as median_unpaid_debt,
--percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by unpaid_debt) as perc75_unpaid_debt,
--percentile_cont(0.9) within group (order by unpaid_debt) as perc90_unpaid_debt,
--percentile_cont(0.95) within group (order by unpaid_debt) as perc95_unpaid_debt 
from base{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:61a72a8d6d002b006bdc2a9d] - my thoughts are set out below. *KEY POINTS:*

(1) To agreed ‘heads of terms’ with Petrobras it is essential to agreed the duration of the arrangement and understand the commercial basis on which it can be terminated. This needs to be raised with them as part of this process now (before we get to any contract drafting / negotiation).

(2) The arrangement seems quite complex, particularly the need to (a) provide ongoing driver lists and (b) use a third party to verify discounts. Is this necessary? It makes sense to avoid the administration and costs if possible, perhaps by making this a basic ‘discount card’ type arrangement.

----

As a starting point, the following elements really need to be considered commercially as part of this ‘heads of terms’ exercise as they will give the arrangement structure:

*(i) Duration?:* How long is the agreement to initially last? How can it be renewed?

*(ii) What would permit the arrangement to be terminated by either party?:* What are Petrobras and Bolt’s requirements? Obviously if there is no cost to Bolt for our drivers recieving the discounts, we may not need to be too concerned with this. But we’ll want to know what Petrobras are expecting.

^^^You’ll want to consider this and ask the same of Petrobras, to understand their requirements.

The third requirement is *(iii) Cost*: Are there any costs being paid by one party to the other? The agreement is silent on this, but presumably the benefit to Petrobras is that they get more customers and therefore no money is being paid to Petrobras by Bolt.

All of the above are generic points for any commercial arrangement, but we should expect this to be agreed before we move to preparing any contracts.

As for the proposal itself, at face value it seems complicated and I am not sure why the complexity is necessary:

(1) There is reference to Bolt providing Petrobras with a list of drivers. Aside from data concerns, it would be much simpler for drivers to simply evidence that they are entitled to discounts in a standard manner i.e. showing their Bolt app, or a ‘discount card’. Is there any reason that a simpler arrangement cannot be reached?

(2) I do not understand the reference in the document to amounts of discounts being verified by a third party - what relevance this is supposed to have? It should be very easy for Petrobras to verify the sum of the discounts that have been given over a given period. 

On both points, something as basic as “show your discount card/App and your matching ID, get *at least* 5% off” seems far more workable. Petrobras could agree that discounts increase the more it is used (which already seems to be the intention).

Finally, I’ve also uploaded the proposal document [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FtN4F90xDwsAt0J2Ff0pDDsy7EoaXPus/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=103938628683900310458&rtpof=true&sd=true] for quick reference. I’d added some short comments with correspond with my thoughts as I read it, but the main points of concern are set out in this reply.

Many thanks.

Investigating why [/internal/getActiveOrdersIds|http://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/33IO6UyZz/delivery-order-client-monitor?viewPanel=106] has a high response time:

The endpoint was created a couple of month ago as an alternative to {{internal/getActiveOrders}} endpoint that internally is executing a pretty complex SQL query with 12 joins. See [this jira task|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/FDO-3335] for details. The endpoint is used in 2 place:

* In {{src/delivery/eater/delivery_eater_order/main/service/OrderService.ts:204}}: the response is used only to pick the ids of active orders - this is making more than 90% of the calls to  endpoint - around {{110 - 120K calls / hour}} at peek hours → external endpoint {{"/deliveryClient/getActiveOrders"}}
* In {{common/customer_support/prioritization/DeliveryEaterRecentOrderService.ts:38}}: the response is used only to determine whether an eater has active orders or not

The endpoint functionality is pretty straight-forward → a single simple query that has no joins.

{noformat}SELECT
  orderT.id as order_id,
  orderT.city_id as city_id
FROM
  `order` orderT
WHERE
  orderT.state IN (
    'waiting_acceptance',
    'waiting_starting_preparation',
    'waiting_preparation',
    'waiting_delivery',
    'ready_for_pickup'
  )
  AND orderT.master_user_id = 14211105
  AND orderT.creator = 'user'
  AND orderT.city_id IN (18, 54, 55, 136, 137, 320, 1153){noformat}

Moreover, both {{master_user_id}} and {{state}} columns are indexed, so from my perspective the query should be fast and optimised.  

When looking at the [PMM query analysis|http://pmm2.sqldb/graph/d/pmm-qan/pmm-query-analytics?var-environment=All&var-cluster=delivery&var-replication_set=All&var-database=All&var-schema=taxify_delivery_order&var-node_name=All&var-service_name=All&var-client_host=All&var-username=All&var-service_type=All&var-node_type=All&var-city=All&var-az=All&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&columns=%5B%22load%22,%22num_queries%22,%22query_time%22%5D&group_by=queryid&filter_by=E1B2A6176A4ABAF0&order_by=-load&from=now-2d&to=now&dimensionSearchText=orderT.master_user_id&page_number=1&page_size=25&totals=false&query_selected&details_tab=details] we can see that the average execution time over the last 2 days is ~113ms with an average of row examined 45 and at most 1 row returned per query.

However, when looking at [node monitor|http://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/33IO6UyZz/delivery-order-client-monitor?orgId=1&refresh=1m&from=now-2d&to=now&viewPanel=106], we see that at peak time the p95 duration is around 5-700ms with p99 even spiking above 5s once. 

My first impressions are:

* There is no optimisation issue or complex query issue
* The problem seems to be the increased DB load during peak-hours that translates to this high response time
* An hypothesis arise from the fact that both {{getActiveOrdersByIds}}  an {{getLightOrdersByIds}} produce a high load on DB due to the huge number of queries more than *4k queries per minute combined at peak hours* → if we reduce the load from {{getLightOrdersByIds}}, then the overall DB load should reduce → increased response time for both endpoints (TO BE CHECKED)
* Starting from the previous point, both queries seems to go the master db node an idea is to move the {{getLightOrdersByIds}} to the slave-db nodes since its about history data witch should already be sync among all db instances.

Investigating high response time for {{internal/getLightOrdersByIds}}: 
Premise: reduce the number of orders for which the history details are retrieved to 45 and based on the result implement pagination. We went with this approach since there are clients that have more than 100-150 orders and retrieving all of them is costly. since the details are retrieved using a query with 6 joins. 

I tested the premise in live environment for 1:30h from 12:30 - 14:00. 

!Screenshot 2022-09-01 at 13.51.00.png|width=2560,height=1440!

!Screenshot 2022-09-01 at 13.50.40.png|width=2560,height=1440!

!Screenshot 2022-09-01 at 13.51.26.png|width=2560,height=1440!

!Screenshot 2022-09-01 at 13.51.40.png|width=2560,height=1440!

As one can see from the graphs above, there was no significant impact in the response time when the number of orders processed was reduced. 

!Screenshot 2022-09-01 at 15.41.14.png|width=2560,height=1440!

When looking at query details, as expected the number of rows examined and sent, decreased, but the average query execution time was not significantly affected. Also, the number of warnings regarding the endpoint duration per request / query duration stayed the same when compared with the last 24h 

!Screenshot 2022-09-01 at 15.44.20.png|width=2560,height=1440!

As a result, the premise may be good, but not good enough to make a significant change in the response time of the {{internal/getLightOrdersByIds}} endpoint

Potential project ideas with overall impact (WIP):

* Compliancy-related processes
** Main focus on ensuring PA as such (by utilizing Performance Management) and potentially streamlining processes to make them more comprehensible, but not necessarily changing the process as it’s defined by regulations
** Impact => protection from regulation breaches
* Processes that are often not adhered to and replaced by custom/local processes
** Main focus on finding out the root cause and why agents do not follow the process → cooperation with the Content team to find out an efficient solution; if process is optimal already, reinforcing it with the agents
** There is usually a reason for agents replacing procedures with custom ones - is the process too complicated, is it because “we always did it that way”, is it because they feel like they can get better CSAT (because they don’t see the bigger picture of why the process is in a certain way)
** Impact => improving our processes and making it easier for our agents and for the customer to get a solution
* Processes that are often followed incorrectly or not fully
** Will typically lead to a misunderstanding of the process → we may need to clarify some steps in the process as such or make a training
** Impact => improving the processes and agent knowledge, leading to ultimately fulfilling the purpose of the process in the first place

Hey Julien

This is what the lawyers sent me about termination process in Malta ([~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e] FYI from WH Partners):

Hi Ioana,

 

Further to your email please find below a general overview in relation to dismissal in Malta.

 

An employer in Malta may only terminate a contract of employment on the basis of:

 

* a good and sufficient cause – a term which has no statutory definition and which constitutes the interpretational basis for each case of unfair dismissal brought before the Industrial Tribunal.
redundancy, or
the employee reaching retirement age.

 

In cases where employment is terminated for good and sufficient cause, the employer is not required to give advance notice of termination and/or pay the employee for any wages relating to such notice period or the unexpired period of a definite term agreed upon. Typically, the employer would be expected to provide a very compelling reason for the dismissal of any employee on this ground, particularly more so when the dismissal is not preceded by any verbal or written disciplinary warnings given by the employer to the employee over a period before the dismissal. Two written warnings given by the employer over a reasonable period of time prior to the final warning and contemporaneous dismissal should serve to demonstrate a degree of prudence on the part of the employer if such dismissal is challenged by the employee as unfair.

 

Therefore if you wish to terminate Darrel immediately my advice would be - unless Liisa disagrees:

* check with lawyers if the issues you have put down here would class as a good and sufficient cause. If yes, then we pay nothing as the employer is not required to give advance notice of termination and/or pay the employee for any wages relating to such notice period
* if lawyers advise it will not constitute good and sufficient cause, then we will ask to help us draw up a settlement agreement. Usually the amount to settle on can be 2-3 months salaries.

I will proceed with checking with the lawyers if the issues can class as good and sufficient cause and update you further

*Results:*
We split the whole group into two samples of size 43k.
Control group had 608 conversions, test group  - 656 conversions,
Conversion rates are 1,5% and 1,39% accordingly.
So the uplift is 0,11pp (or 7,5%.)

*Are the results robust (will repeat in the future)?*

Currently we do not have evidence to say they are robust.

Standard t-test shows p-value of 0,17 (would expect less than 0,05),
Our true uplift could be in the range of \[-0.03, 0.19] (including 0, so could as well be no effect)

This is partly because out of 43k users in control, only 17k were reached by Facebook.
So the effect could be higher if we could reach more users. One idea here could to probably try other channels here together with FB. Karina, what do you think about GDN?

To be more sure about the robustness, we could have another experiment (and then combine the results).

*Are the results interesting from business perspective?*

One might think that 0,12pp growth is not something that we expect.

But on the other hand, in this experiment we got additional 50 orders at the cost of 400 Eur. The AOV (in terms of price) for orders in test group is 24 Eur. So Revenue to cost is 50*24 = 1200 to 400.

Hey [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7], sure. The European [Commission Notice |https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:52021XC1229(06)&from=EN]on Article 6a (price reduction article) of Omnibus Directive says: _In contrast, Article 6a does not apply to the intermediaries that provide the mere means for traders to sell their products (13), such as online marketplaces, or that merely aggregate and display information about the prices provided by other sellers (price comparison platforms). These intermediaries remain subject to the general rules on intermediary liability and professional diligence obligations._ 

Thus, if all member states implemented Omnibus price reduction rules in a way described in the Notice, price reduction rules would not have applied to the online marketplaces (just to restaurants and stores) acting on our platform.

Gentlemen, 

There are two matters here.

# What is good for the long-term business
# What is good for the short-term business

Short-term allowing 16+ use may create a boon in activity, it will also however carry a corresponding cost for the business at statistically those users are 2 to 3x more likely to have incidents.

MTPL insurance being bereft of exclusions will have to meet with those claims and, long-term that cost will be reflected back to the operator through increased premiums.

So considering purely the financial impact of the increased incident of claims 16 and 17 year olds would produce I question why we are insistent on serving this portion of the market.

When considered more broadly, those incidents will also attract more media and public attention when the injuries are fatal or grave, i.e. was profit placed ahead of public safety in electing to allow 16 and 17 yo use.

With respect to underage use, to be clear, we cannot prevent it, if someone wants to register with false ID, or some such, or just lie about their age, there is only so much we can or need to do. Once they are on the scooter it becomes an issue between the user, the law, and insurers. 

I believe that both VOI and Tier are wrong by the way, the insurance would respond to any claim presented irrespective of the age of the user, this is an EU wide obligation in respect of MTPL coverages, i.e. there cannot be an uninsured injury to a third party. The difference is that they would then seek remedy against the liable party, in this case the child or their parents.

In summary, I personally don’t advocate for U18 use because I believe that this would increase our claims experience which will ultimately increase our costs. In time as the units become more familiar to cities and users then perhaps that risk will become more wearable but I believe short term it is a source of costs we are better to avoid.

DEKRA NL legal team has informed that:

Article 4 (iv): if the disclosing party discloses certain information to a third party without confidentiality obligations, then why would the same information be subject to confidentiality obligations for the receiving party? Clearly, the information is at that point not deemed to be confidential anymore. Please note: it only applies to the same piece of information, not to all information\!

Article 4 (v): This just gives the possibility to give the authorization to send certain information to a third party. We do not see why Bolt would want to remove this? If Bolt does not want the information to go the third party, Bold simply does not give its permission to do so. This just creates the possibility of being able to transfer information if necessary. For example, we sometimes get information requests by foreign custom authorities to supply them with a testing report. This means we would be able to do so, but only in case Bolt gives us the permission to do so.

*TL; DR* Let’s

* drop Groundscope templates in full;
* move forward with our new standard template only, and 
* have them suggest precise changes to our template should they deem it relevant.

_Their draft seems to designed foremost for small-mid sized taxi/coach companies and other transportation service providers over whom they have full bargaining power. Unlike our draft, which is:_

* _leaner,_ 
* _more straightforward (it’s strictly about what’s relevant for the integration), and_ 
* _balanced (parties rights and obligations are on par unless context strictly requires otherwise)._



*In few more words why we should disregard their docs in full:*
*Their* [*Partner T&C* |https://groundscope.co.uk/service-partner-terms-conditions/]has the exact same object as our API template meaning that some conflict is already embedded. We could consider adding theirs as appendix to ours only if theirs is safe and largely matches ours _(though I do not recommend this to start with as it will open up room for dispute in each case)_. However this is not the case here. Far from it. 

To summarize some of the issues:

* SLA’s;

# Do we really accept SLA’s and similar? See the schedules “Services & Charges”, “Service Partner prices and rates”  “Service Partner Service Level Agreement” and “Deductions”
# Even if yes, we shouldn’t allow GS to amend these unilaterally as they please.

* GS clients, i.e business clients brought in as parties with directly enforceable rights against us based on the Partner T&C (c 12.3);

Also, GS claims to act as the disclosed agent of their Clients _- typically especially aggregators wish to distance themselves from their clients._ It shouldn’t play into our standard, but should be evaluated strictly if theirs was used, e.g GS would liable for the payment to us, not the User (c 5.3), also plays into personal data processing setup.

* Bolt as a transportation service provider, see e.g. 3.2, 3.5, 3.8 (full liability for driver and vehicle compliance);
* Wide rights for GS to unilaterally instruct us, e.g c 3.1. Furthermore change the terms of the T&C unilaterally (c 12.1);
* Bolt’s obligation to provide all relevant registration documents and whatnot, and send any updated doc over to GS pro-actively - admin burden (see c 3.4);
* parties rights&obligations are not overall on par - see e.g. clause 2 vs 3, also 6.4, 6.5, 6.6, 11, 12.2, 12.5;
* GS liability for payment limited to what they have received from their clients, etc (5.3,5.4);
* Heavy requirements for insurance 3.7 - though I believe we largely meet the requirements as to our UK business;
* C 6.3 - safety is on us. How much should safety also be of GS's issue considering all goes down in their ecosystem?
* inaccurate terms, e.g. “Driver” is neither Bolt’s employee or a sub-contractor; also “Services” as provided by Bolt are not transportation services as such;
* Term and termination (c 8) - That's different from our standard, but I guess roughly ok though drafted (again) keeping foremost GS's interests in mind. Also, what’s actually the intended Term of the Agreement (see 1.1)?
* C 12.4 - removal from each other platforms. Tbc if viable;
* Irrelevant terms included, e.g about booking of coaches;
* confusing terms included, e.g.

1. Is our “Booking fee” or “Service Fee” meant under the “Service Partner Charges”?

2. What does “reasonable assistance” under 2.2 entail? 

3. Clause 2.3 - can we provide this via API?

4. prices/rates (c 3.9) - not clear if the same idea is reached as with our standard template, see also the obligation to “send over” the updated rates (and at least 30 days prior notice before changing them). See also c 5.1 which is unclear.

5. C 6.2 - could be read so that any such co-op would always include also reducing charges.

6. 10.1 What is “confirmed electronic transmission”? Email?

Considering my overall suggestion how to take these negotiations forward then no resources have been allocated at this point to reviewing some further boilerplate such as confidentiality, force majeure. Also privacy. Also might require a local counsel check to fully grasp the scope of some of the clauses, e.g. 3.6.



*As to their other documents*, i.e 

* the [Booking Policy|https://groundscope.co.uk/booking-terms/], _which should be entered into by Bolt and a client/demand partner in relation to each reservation made by a client and accepted by Bolt_ then these overlap with our Terms of Service between Bolt and User, and same principal issues occur as described above. Fundamentally rides would happen on service provider’s - which is Bolt - terms.
* As to their [compliance requirement|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1luIveIZi3KWIOxSL0A8j2vMLWptR14Ga/edit]s then as long as these were strictly about Bolt’s responsibilities then could be accepted but everything else must be on best endeavour basis (regards to driver compliance etc, see e.g. 2.3). Also, no point in overlap with the core agreements.

And as with the Partner T&C, we should not accept unilateral changes to be done to these docs by GS.

Hi [~accountid:6201340d6ba61b006fb48b54] , thank you. Please find my answers below - feel free to share this with Dekra.

*Article 4 (iv):* What we don’t like about this provision is that it gives room to a mistake committed by Bolt (disclosing confidential information to a third party without a proper NDA or confidentiality obligations in place) being used to justify a potential breach of confidentiality on Dekra’s side (disclose of information that under the NDA between Bolt and Dekra is deemed confidential). Note that, if the information in question becomes public available, it would already be exempted by the NDA in view of clause 4(ii).

*Article 4 (v):* If that’s the purpose of the clause, it's already captured by the next paragraph reproduced here: “Furthermore, DEKRA shall be authorized to provide Confidential Information to third parties on the basis of the applicable conditions of the relevant accreditation or designation of DEKRA as a certifying institution. Likewise, in the event that certification is to be performed by a third party based on an assessment by DEKRA, DEKRA shall be authorized to provide Confidential Information to that third party.”

Nevertheless, if Dekra still deem article 4 (v) necessary, we suggest that it’s rephrased as follows: “is removed from confidential status or cleared for disclosure to a third party, +in both cases specifically in the context and for the purposes of this Agreement+, by prior written consent of a duly authorised officer of the disclosing party, subject to any conditions which may be provided for at the time of such removal or clearance.” The current wording also gives room for an arrangement between Bolt and a third party being used in case Dekra breaches its confidentiality obligations.

Thank you for clarification [~accountid:61c2f85f90cfd20071570ff8] ,

So, first things first, billing model has nothing to do with the payment method. Payment method depends on whether they are a Credit Card company or a Postpaid company (which in their case is a Postpaid company). But Postpaid companies can have 2 different payment methods (#2, #3 below):

# *Credit Card company*: Each ride is captured separately from their Credit Card. They get an invoice for each specific ride. And they get a statement at the end of the month. However, the point is that they get charged one by one for each ride.
# *Postpaid*: Rides are not charged individually. The bulk amount is invoiced at the end of the month and the client makes a bank transfer. 
# *Postpaid Credit Card*: Same scenario as #2 except as they added a credit card, the bulk amount is charged automatically on the due date instead of a bank transfer - AND they get a monthly invoice.

*Billing Methods*:

* *Intermediary*: User invoices (individual invoices for each ride) should be used for accounting purposes.
* *Resale*: Monthly aggregated invoice should be used for accounting purposes.

So, from your description, I understand that the company is currently on #3. So they already get charged on the due date and get a monthly invoice for it. Please note they will still get individual user invoices as we, Bolt, need to invoice every service. But in resale model, this invoice is between Bolt and the driver so there is no need for the business to use these individual invoices for reporting purposes. They can simply only consider the aggregated invoice.

So, if I got your question right, based on the explanation above, yes this model is possible.

Every scenario that which Fraud denies user deletion is covered in the KB article. Please check it => [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360003841794|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360003841794]

Keep in mind that IMD uses an in memory cache that updated using a local lock cron. This mean that you can have 2 service instances i-v-p1 and i-v-p2 and i-v-p1 already have new data (refreshed the cache) and i-v-p2 still use the old data. If you have some complex operation that executes partially on i-v-p1 and then on i-v-p2 and required data from flow you might get into weird behaviours and not understand what happened.



Not saying IMD is not a good solution, just that we should keep this in mind.

Copied from [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4048027665/2022-09-02+-+Improving+Chaos+Testing+Tooling|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4048027665/2022-09-02+-+Improving+Chaos+Testing+Tooling|smart-link]: 

*Problems:*

# When reducing 6 services down to 1 they + database can often handle the load except for just the configuration of database pool which we can only define per service and it should be increased 6x so everything works again. Is that a positive finding that we should increase the pool size or does it show that our configuration is set up in a wrong way? Do we expect the service to db connection pool to belong to a single service or a database? On each release we also loose 1/6 (or even 1/3) of the capacity which is sometimes dangerous. If we want to scale up/down services is it because of CPU and I/O of NodeJS or is it because we want to get more db connections? Often more DB connections doesn’t mean we need more service instances as well.
# So far chaos testing sessions were focusing only on the backend NodeJS services but our DriverX scaling bottlenecks issues are related to databases. E.g.
# Chaos testing is only done once per year traditionally for preparing for NYE. However the risk of NYE in particular has decreased significantly. It only affects Ride-hailing as it’s off season for scooters, only little deliveries are done on nights etc. In ride-hailing we now have many different time zones so any spikes from a year switch are spread between them. Overall the original reasoning for chaos testing seems outdated. Testing is still important. Why not automate it better and do it more often throughout the year. Once a year for us means the number of devs and services could already grow 1.5-2x which maybe leaves too long gaps.
# So far we have only reduced capacities which is not testing what we actually want - more load.
# Chaos testing only takes use of Live environment.

*Ideas for solutions:*

# Consider re-defining service to db connection pool size concept so it’s a single value for all n services. Each service would only get 1/n of the pool size.
# Reduce capacity of database (or ProxySQL or connection from NodeJS). E.g. less CPU, I/O throughput, lag, smaller pool sizes etc.
# We could identity which read-only requests we could produce load on.
# We could implement so called shadow orders which test the whole flow but don’t affect end users functionally.
# Instead of running it during dedicated sessions keep a 24/7 running (with pauses) bot to test our system (e.g. take down services etc).
# Instead of taking a resource offline we could mimic situation of network lag or partial packet loss.
# We could synthesize crappy request data.
# We could automate request generation to all endpoints (in staging).

Alright that changes things since the contract is structured as if we are the contracting party for the insurances. We would need to make quite a lot of changes in order to reflect this, here are some comments from my side: 

* Clause 2.1: “Söderberg & Partners åtar sig att göra en utredning av Uppdragsgivarens önskemål och behov av skadeförsäkring.” This doesn’t correctly describe what we aim to do with S&P, we don’t want to review whether we need insurance, only assist our fleets and see if they want insurance. Description of object of the contract needs to be revised. 
* Clause 2.5: “Söderberg & Partners åtar sig därefter att ombesörja att avtal om försäkring ingås mellan Uppdragsgivaren och valt/valda försäkringsgivare”. No insurance contract shall be entered into by Bolt itself - hence this needs to be worded differently. 
* Clause 2.6: “Söderberg & Partners åtar sig att årligen gå igenom försäkringsskyddet med Uppdragsgivaren, såvida inte behov av genomgång saknas.” Again, should be in relation to the fleets and not Bolt. 
* Clause 3:1 “Uppdragsgivaren ansvarar i förhållande till Söderberg & Partners för att underlagen och uppgifterna är aktuella, korrekta och tillförlitliga”. We do not want to be responsible for that information provided for the insurance coverage is correct since the information is not in relation to our business, this should be the fleets. 
* Clause 3.3: “Uppdragsgivaren åtar sig att på eget initiativ, d.v.s. även utan särskild förfrågan, till Söderberg & Partners lämna uppgift om förhållanden av uppenbar betydelse för riskbedömningen”. Same here as above, should not be our responsibility. 
* Clause 4: “Ersättning till Söderberg & Partners baseras på den/de försäkringspremier som Uppdragsgivaren betalar för de försäkringar som ingås till följd av Avtalet” As mentioned by you this wording does not work since Bolt does not pay any insurance premiums. 

I could reference all clauses that do not work based on this set-up but I would rather suggest that you revert to S&P that the agreement needs to be reviewed and it needs to be clarified throughout the agreement that the responsibilities lie with the fleets, that Bolt does not enter into any insurances and that no costs are paid by us. We are merely an intermediary here in order to get fleets informed and ready to obtain insurance coverage. The current agreement is worded as if we are obtaining insurance from them, that we are providing the information for the risk assessment of the insurances and responsible for doing this in a correct way etc. 

Best regards,
