COUNT(DISTINCT (CASE WHEN (co.is_chargeback = 1 OR co.is_final_failed_payment = 1 OR co.is_payment_problem = 1 OR (CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.refund_amount*1.0/co.user_price END)>0.8) THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_fraud_order,
ROUND(CASE WHEN count_orders > 0 THEN count_fraud_order*1.0/count_orders END,2) AS count_ratio,
ROUND(SUM(co.user_price_eur),2) AS sum_GMV,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (co.is_chargeback = 1 OR co.is_final_failed_payment = 1 OR co.is_payment_problem = 1 OR (CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.refund_amount*1.0/co.user_price END)>0.8) THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_fraud,
ROUND(CASE WHEN sum_GMV > 0 THEN sum_fraud*1.0/sum_GMV END,2) AS amount_ratio, 
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type = 'business' THEN co.order_id END) AS count_business_orders, 
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bl.business_company_id IS NOT NULL THEN co.order_id END) AS count_business_deactivated, 
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bl.reason = 'fraud' THEN co.order_id END) AS count_business_fraud,
ROUND(CASE WHEN count_business_orders > 0 THEN count_business_deactivated*1.0/count_business_orders END,2) AS business_deactivated_ratio,
ROUND(CASE WHEN count_business_orders > 0 THEN count_business_fraud*1.0/count_business_orders END,2) AS business_fraud_ratio,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type = 'business' THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_business_GMV,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN bl.business_company_id IS NOT NULL THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_business_deactivated,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN bl.reason = 'fraud' THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_business_fraud,
ROUND(CASE WHEN sum_business_GMV > 0 THEN sum_business_deactivated*1.0/sum_business_GMV END,2) AS business_deactivated_sum_ratio,
ROUND(CASE WHEN sum_business_GMV > 0 THEN sum_business_fraud*1.0/sum_business_GMV END,2) AS business_fraud_sum_ratio,
COUNT(DISTINCT (CASE WHEN co.rider_discount > 0 THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_order_with_campaign,
ROUND(SUM(co.rider_discount/co.eur_currency_rate),2) AS campaign_sum_eur,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.rider_discount > 0 THEN co.partner_price_eur END),2) AS sum_driver_price_order_with_campaign, 
ROUND(CASE WHEN sum_driver_price_order_with_campaign > 0 THEN campaign_sum_eur*1.0/sum_driver_price_order_with_campaign END,2) AS ratio_covered_by_campaign, 
COUNT(DISTINCT (CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback = 1 THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_chargeback_order,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback = 1 THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_chargeback_order,
COUNT(DISTINCT (CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = 1 THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_failed_payment_order,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = 1 THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_failed_payment_order,
COUNT(DISTINCT (CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem = 1 THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_payment_problem_order,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem = 1 THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_payment_problem_order,
COUNT(DISTINCT (CASE WHEN (CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.refund_amount*1.0/co.user_price END)>0.8 THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_refunded_order,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.refund_amount*1.0/co.user_price END)>0.8 THEN co.refund_amount/co.eur_currency_rate END),2) AS sum_refunded_order
FROM etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
LEFT JOIN business_business_company_deactivation_log bl ON split_part(co.payment_method_id, '-', 1) = bl.business_company_id 
LEFT JOIN company_order_try ot ON co.order_id = ot.order_id AND co.city_id = ot.city_id 
LEFT JOIN fleet_driver fd ON fd.id = ot.driver_id 
LEFT JOIN fleet_driver_root fdr ON fdr.id = fd.driver_root_id
WHERE co.order_try_state = 'finished'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'

--AND ot.driver_id = 3159248
AND fd.company_id = 44655
AND co.created >= '2022-04-04'
GROUP BY 1 {code}

As a general rule, from a tax perspective, the cost of assets or services should be borne by the entity that effectively will use that asset or service. 

In the present case, I understand that the service will be used by Bolt Market LEs and, as such, the cost should be with those entities. Therefore, the agreement should normally be concluded between the service provider and the respective Bolt Market local entities (e.g. Bolt Market EE) using their local VAT numbers. The VAT numbers for Bolt entities are available [*here*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TAX/pages/1850245987/TAX+VAT+registration+numbers+Certificates+of+Tax+Residency].  

In this instance, our preference would be to have separate agreements for the individual Bolt Market local entities (i.e. one with Bolt Market EE and another one with Bolt Market LT). Alternatively, the contract could be concluded between the service provider and Bolt Operations OU (using its Estonian VAT number) who would then recharge this cost to the Bolt Market LEs accordingly. The former approach would be neater and more straightforward from a tax perspective. Please refer to the general guidelines for procurement of assets and services for tax purposes [*here*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/13_j1EmhmE00K0-esg0s6IFG8DbpY7304XyFA5LCT1Fs/edit?usp=sharing]*.* 

There should not be any adverse tax consequences arising from the payments being made by Bolt Store EE (or Bolt Operations OU) to the Lithuanian service provider on the basis that these payments are business related and are paid based on valid VAT invoices issued by the service provider but [~accountid:5eda5d0647291b0b8608735a] and [~accountid:61641a302f6aed0068fb7b50] please shout as needed.

Discrepancies in Prophet forecasts between different systems is a known issue and actually not an issue, but just the way existing model works:
[https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/253|https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/253|smart-link] 
[https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/411|https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/411|smart-link] 
[https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/1077|https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/1077|smart-link] 
Basic fitting means finding MAP estimate and initial parameters are sampled from different prior distributions. By default Stan backend used L-BFGS which is a quasi-Newton optimization algorithm to get this estimate.


When I switched Stan backend to use Newton algorithm directly then forecasts were matching exactly between my local env and CI-CD pipeline. Therefore, my best guess is that approximating Hessian in L-BFGS is where platform level float precision starts to play role. When using Newton algo we compute Hessian on each step directly and therefore solution results in the same model parameters which lead to the exact same forecast (at least in my case). Note, however, that Newton scales as O(N^3) and is considerably slow (6x on my data) (L-BFGS is O(N^2)).

Problem:

Gnss receiver needs to know detailed information about constellation - satellites status and exact locations, plus recise time.

This information consists of three parts - current time, almamac and ephemeris. Almanac includes low-resolution orbital information about satellites and their status. Epheperis includes precide information about satellites.

This information is sent by satellites as part of the feed over radio, but data rate here is rather slow - ca 50 bits/sec - and especially in weak signal condition lost packets may require restart of reception. Transmission of full almanac over the radio takes 10+ minutes per constellation.

Having this information available to the received by other means makes acquiring the initial fix (TTFF - time to first fix) faster when the receiver is cold-started and on some cases may improve precision in weak-signal conditions.

Solution:

We use ublox and quectel gnss received modules in CU and CQ series iots correspondingly. Both manufacturers have their own solutions to get this information. Ublox service is called AssistNow. In older iots (R9/R11/R20 we use quectel MC60 with integrated gnss module, and this module requires agnss information directly from quectel, when data connection is established, the transmission being outside of user (our) control)

To distribute the agnss information to iots we publish it on the mqtt (with retain=true) where each device which needs it can subscribe and receive it. We use /agnss/q/ prefix for quectel and /agnss/u/ prefix for ublox information.

There is balance between size of the data block and frequency it has to be published. For quectel we filter the data received and include only messages relevant for += 2h from current time, plus we add time-hint message, and publish this each 10 seconds. The high frequency allows device to always get precise-enough time-hint, when needed.

Reference implementation:

[https://github.com/bolteu/tools/blob/master/iot-mngmt/iot_service/agnss.js|https://github.com/bolteu/tools/blob/master/iot-mngmt/iot_service/agnss.js] 

additional information:

[https://www.u-blox.com/en/product/assistnow|https://www.u-blox.com/en/product/assistnow|smart-link] 
[https://www.quectel.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Quectel_LC29D_AGNSS_Application_Note_V1.0.pdf|https://www.quectel.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Quectel_LC29D_AGNSS_Application_Note_V1.0.pdf]

{code:sql}SELECT
country_code,
order_id,
oo_order_start,
oo_order_end,
user_id,
payment_method_group,
user_price,
user_price_eur,
bolt_credit,
bolt_credit_eur,
fraud_label,
uncovered_amount_eur,
card_country,
card_age,
device_age,
user_age,
COUNT(parallel_order_id)-1 AS count_of_parallel_orders,
SUM(parallel_order_price_eur)-user_price_eur AS sum_of_parallel_orders_eur
FROM (
	SELECT DISTINCT
	country_code,
	order_id,
	oo_order_start,
	oo_order_end,
	user_id,
	payment_method_group,
	user_price,
	user_price_eur,
	bolt_credit,
	bolt_credit_eur,
	fraud_label,
	uncovered_amount_eur,
	parallel_order_id,
--	parallel_order_payment_method_group,
	parallel_order_price_eur,
	card_country,
	card_age,
	device_age,
	user_age
	FROM (
		WITH parallel_order AS (
		SELECT DISTINCT --eater_order_states
		etl.user_id,
		etl.order_id,
		etl.payment_method_group,
		etl.user_price/r.rate AS user_price_eur,
		etl.user_price AS user_price,
		sl.created AS order_state_created,
		etl.created AS order_start,
		CASE WHEN sl.to_state='delivered' THEN sl.created ELSE NULL END AS order_end
		FROM etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
		LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_state_log AS sl ON sl.order_id=etl.order_id AND sl.city_id=etl.city_id
		LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON etl.price_currency = r.currency AND date_trunc('day', etl.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on)
		WHERE etl.order_type='food_delivery'
		AND etl.order_state='finished'
		AND etl.payment_method_group='in-app'
		UNION ALL
		SELECT DISTINCT --provider_order_states
		etl.user_id,
		etl.order_id,
		etl.payment_method_group,
		etl.user_price/r.rate AS user_price_eur,
		etl.user_price AS user_price,
		sl.created AS order_state_created,
		etl.created AS order_start,
		en.created AS order_end
		FROM etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
		LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_provider_state_log AS sl ON sl.order_id=etl.order_id AND sl.city_id=etl.city_id
		LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_state_log AS en ON en.order_id=etl.order_id AND en.city_id=etl.city_id AND en.to_state='delivered'
		LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON etl.price_currency = r.currency AND date_trunc('day', etl.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on)
		WHERE etl.order_type='food_delivery'
		AND etl.order_state='finished'
		AND etl.payment_method_group='in-app'
		UNION ALL
		SELECT DISTINCT --courier_order_states
		etl.user_id,
		etl.order_id,
		etl.payment_method_group,
		etl.user_price/r.rate AS user_price_eur,
		etl.user_price AS user_price,
		sl.created AS order_state_created,
		etl.created AS order_start,
		CASE WHEN sl.to_state='delivered' THEN sl.created ELSE NULL END AS order_end
		FROM etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
		LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS sl ON sl.order_id=etl.order_id AND sl.city_id=etl.city_id
		LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON etl.price_currency = r.currency AND date_trunc('day', etl.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on)
		WHERE etl.order_type='food_delivery'
		AND etl.order_state='finished'
		AND etl.payment_method_group='in-app'
		),
		original_order AS (
		SELECT DISTINCT --eater_order_states
		sl.city_id,
		sl.order_id,
		sl.created
		FROM delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS sl
		UNION ALL
		SELECT DISTINCT --provider_order_states
		sl.city_id,
		sl.order_id,
		sl.created
		FROM delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS sl
		UNION ALL
		SELECT DISTINCT --courier_order_states
		sl.city_id,
		sl.order_id,
		sl.created
		FROM delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS sl
		)
		SELECT DISTINCT
		etl.country_code,
		etl.order_id,
		etl.created AS oo_order_start,
		sl.created AS oo_order_end,
		po.order_state_created,
		etl.user_id,
		etl.payment_method_group,
		etl.user_price,
		etl.user_price/r.rate AS user_price_eur,
		etl.bolt_credit_captured_amount AS bolt_credit,
		etl.bolt_credit_captured_amount/r.rate AS bolt_credit_eur,
		CASE WHEN etl.fraud_label=TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS fraud_label,
		etl.uncovered_amount/r.rate AS uncovered_amount_eur,
		po.order_id AS parallel_order_id,
		po.payment_method_group AS parallel_order_payment_method_group,
		po.user_price_eur AS parallel_order_price_eur,
		COALESCE(etl.card_country,rd.card_country) AS card_country,
		COALESCE(DATEDIFF('day',pmu.created,etl.created),rd.card_age_in_days) AS card_age,
		rd.user_device_created_age_in_days AS device_age,
		DATEDIFF('day',u.created,etl.created) AS user_age
		FROM etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
		LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_state_log AS sl ON sl.order_id=etl.order_id AND sl.city_id=etl.city_id AND sl.to_state='delivered'
		LEFT JOIN original_order AS oo ON oo.city_id=etl.city_id AND oo.order_id=etl.order_id
		LEFT JOIN parallel_order AS po ON po.user_id=etl.user_id AND (po.order_state_created BETWEEN etl.created AND sl.created OR oo.created BETWEEN po.order_start AND po.order_end)
		LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON etl.price_currency = r.currency AND date_trunc('day', etl.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on)
		LEFT JOIN pii.etl_archive_analytical_delivery_order_request_data AS rd ON rd.id=etl.fraud_calculation_id
		LEFT JOIN payment_payment_method_user AS pmu ON pmu.card_alias=etl.card_alias AND pmu.payment_method_id=etl.payment_method_id AND etl.payment_user_id=pmu.payment_user_id

2. Picker won’t show on the planned shift without prior notice. For such a case we’ve agreed:
 - We have to inform them if such an event occurs. We have 1 hour to do it (counted from 1st hour in which picker was expected);
 - They have maximum 3 hours to find the replacement for given picker
 - If they will not find the replacement within a given time, they are obligated to pay a fine of 200 PLN for each hour, on which the contractor is absent. Fine calculation starts after this 3 hours i.e picker was planned to come at 8 AM -> we need to inform agency until 9 AM -> Agency has time until 11 AM to find the replacement -> If they fail, we start to charge calculation from 11 AM
 - For such a case I propose clause “_If the Contractor will not show on the planned shift, without prior notice, the Agency is obligated to find a replacement for given Contractor within 3 hours, counted from the hour in which this Contractor was expected to start. Bolt is obligated to inform Agency if such an event occur within 1 hour. If the Agency will not find the replacement for the Contractor within mentioned 3 hours, Agency is obligated to pay a fine in the amount of 200 (two hundred) PLN for each hour, on which the Contractor is absent.”_ (*This is also agreed with our partner)*

Yes, they did check the verification article, but the issue doesn’t align with the current ticket issue description: “Rental user reports issues during the automated verification process; needs to update their licence or add a new one; has questions about the process”. They are not having an issue with verification, not trying to update their licence or add a new one. They are contacting CS because their spouse/partner/friend got blocked on Bolt Drive due to having verified their personal driving licence to another person’s account. Their personal account isn’t blocked, so even if they check the verification article or the blocking article it doesn’t mean they have this issue themselves. 

For context, in August we blocked 2500+ users for verifying their licences on other people’s account, which was a system flaw of Jumio, our previous verification platform. The blocked users contacted us asking about the issue, we asked for an explanation and proceeded with the unblocking IF the users only verified their licence to 2 accounts max and had a valid reason for it (+ we deleted their licence from other account before the unblocking). Hi [~accountid:60e01bcd7536500070d50663], 

As you are aware the marketing regulation is quite strict in Sweden and in order to be compliant we need to be careful with our marketing strategies. Regarding this set-up: 

* +Payment+: Are we getting paid for this marketing campaign that we would be doing for the third party? What is our incentive to do this? 
* +Responsibility+: Although the marketing is done on behalf of a third party we are responsible as if we were doing it on behalf of ourselves. Hence. we need to follow all guidelines even in cases where we aren’t selling our own products or services. 
* +Transparency+: It needs to be clear that this offer is a marketing campaign and it needs to be stated who is responsible for the marketing. If we do not mention the third party, the recipient will assume that it is a marketing campaign of Bolt which may be interpreted as misleading. It is prohibited to use any type of hidden marketing and simply including a link to a third party without mentioning the TP may be considered to be hidden marketing. 
* +Personal Data+: Will the third party receive any personal data through us? It is not permitted to transfer any personal data to a third party without the consent of the driver that is being targeted here for the marketing campaign. We need to ensure that no personal data is transferred though any link or similar. 

Let me know if you need any further guidance on the set-up. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hey, this is the answer we got from local advisors on July 27th. Ops was discussing with them car wrapping questions and suggested to jump in into the conversation with more in-depth marketing questions. Google Translated and advisor answers are in *Bold*:

TL;DR: Using the Bolt brand to promote the taxi category/hailing taxi drivers is risky because the brand is already associated with ride-hailing, so even though the ad is formally a dispatch company, the ad could be considered false.

Question 1: There is a separate legal entity for dispatching activities (Bolt Services LT), while the ridehailing activities are carried out by Bolt Operations OU. If we have that separate company, maybe everything is fine with "taxi drivers"/"taxis"?
Question 2: Advertising in local online and offline channels (Lithuanian FB groups or distribution of flyers, etc.) is paid for by Bolt Services LT, the dispatcher. What will happen from now on - if the advertiser is a dispatcher, can we order general advertising for the Bolt brand there (with logo, etc.)? Can't we just mix the terms "ride" and "taxi" in one ad?

*Answer: The regulation of taxi and ride-hailing activities has not changed, and as Nerijus rightly mentioned, the separation of activities is a very important aspect in order to meet the requirements of legal acts. The words "taxi/taxi drivers" may be used in advertising for the activities of this separate legal entity. However, it must be clear that this entity is not only the customer of the advertisement, but the advertisement is about its activities. Otherwise, there is a risk that the provisions of the advertising law will be violated. The biggest problem is that the Bolt brand is overwhelmingly associated with a ride-hailing service. Most often, misleading advertising is viewed through the lens of consumers. As we have mentioned in the legal opinions provided to you earlier, the Road Transport Code clearly states that the word "taxi" cannot be used in the operation of a ride-hailing service and vice versa. As we understand from the description of the organization of the taxi advertisement provided by you, Bolt Service LT would not appear anywhere in the advertisement. He would only be an advertiser/payer (in other words, an "accountant/paper" stain). The ad would essentially feature the Bolt branding and slogans inviting taxi drivers to join and/or calling attention to the new taxi category. In the context of Bolt's brand awareness, in our view, the use of the words "taxi/taxi driver" in advertising together with the Bolt brand, as well as the use of the terms "ride" and "taxi" in the same advertisement, are sufficiently risky. A possible solution could be the registration of a separate brand "Bolt Taxi", which would belong to Bolt Services LT and advertising would be organized around taxi dispatching activities, instead of a "mix" of ridehailing and taxi activities.*

Question 3: Can we use the Bolt logo and the word "taxi" in one ad, if the advertising services are ordered by a legal entity performing dispatching activities (Bolt Servies LT)?

*Answer 3: Our comment above kind of answers this question of yours. As we have mentioned, in our opinion, the mere fact that the advertisement is commissioned by a legal entity engaged in taxi dispatching activities does not eliminate the risks associated with illegal/misleading advertising.*

Question 4: Can Bolt Services LT, which now conducts dispatching activities in general, use the Bolt brand in its commissioned advertisements, regardless of the topic of the advertisement.

*Answer 4: As we mentioned above, in our view, the Bolt brand would still be associated with ride-hailing services, which creates the legal risks discussed. A possible solution could be the registration of a separate brand "Bolt Taxi", which would belong to Bolt Services LT.*

My comment: 

Advertising on global channels (Google/FB ads) is paid for by Bolt Operations OÜ, a ride-hailing service provider. Here, it is obvious that no advertisement with the beginnings of a taxi, neither for passengers nor for drivers, will be able to be there as long as the advertisement is ordered by OÜ.

There is a grey area in our system where we send an event to update cash_in_hands after the payInCash transaction finished (i.e. provider finalises the cash payment as successful), even if the courier doesn’t mark the order as “picked”. If the order is not picked by the courier, he/she can be redispatched by customer support. The main concern is that even though the current behaviour looks logically correct (courier 1 pays from debt money, courier 2 doesn't pay anything and picks up the order), we don't know what actually happens in real life (i.e. maybe the provider will hand back the money to the courier).
To avoid any problems, we decided to disallow redispatching if cash payment was made.

First of all, as we have discussed with [~accountid:5f0ea3c39d9a1200294cef2c] some time ago, the loan IC agreements shall be the domain of the Tax team. 

However, as a goodwill gesture I can help you with high-level advice on Cl 8. In Ukrainian legal doctrine there’s a long-term discussion whether 2 Ukrainian parties can have a contract without foreign element governed by foreign law. Prevailing position is that this is forbidden and such a clause shall be null and void. The choice of arbitration body will not be void due to New York Convention, however in practice it will be hard to adjudicate disputes this way and enforce the award. 

Please note that there’re also other issues that might be problematic under UA laws, including: 
- absence of the bank details of the parties
- interest rate is not fixed and it’s not quite clear how it changes over time
- it seems that the loan will be provided upon request - the agreement shall specify how such requests are submitted 
- the loan shall be more detailed no now it is redeemed and repaid 
- it’s recommended to have such contracts in UA language as they may be urgently requested during a tax audit 
- etc.

To summarise the position in relation to promo codes:

* The general rule under the Omnibus is this: whenever we “announce” a price reduction (e.g. showing a strikethrough price in the menu, or “was X, now Y”) we need to ensure the original/reference price is the lowest price from the previous 30 days.

* One exception to this general rule is “loyalty programs”. Our view is that the kind of promo code that you described (user adds it in the profile and then app reacts as if the user is enrolled into campaign with strike through prices on all SKUs) constitutes a “loyalty program” and therefore the general rule above does not apply, subject to two conditions:

# we are targeting only a minority of customers overall (ideally <30%, but there’s no strict definition so it’s a sliding scale risk-wise);
# we include T&Cs at the point that the promo code is added / activated (including e.g. any exclusions / specific terms relating to the promocode).

So, in order to be compliant we need to ensure that the total number of users receiving the promo code is limited to a small % of total users. If not, we can still run the promo code but in this case would need to track the previous 30 days’ prices and ensure we are displaying the correct reference price (in other words - the “general rule” would apply).

h2. *Creating a psychological safety action plan*

To create this plan, all one needs to do is make a simple chart.

# *Learner Safety* (Stop & Start)
# *Collaborator Safety* (Stop & Start)
# *Challenger Safety* (Stop & Start)
# *Inclusion Safety* (Stop & Start)

For each quadrant, consider two actions that will be impactful. One of these actions is to start a new behaviour, and the other activity is to stop a behaviour.

*Learner Safety*

* *Stop:* Assuming everyone is on the same page.
* *Start:* Keep a journal on positive interactions and how to improve next time.

*Collaborator Safety*

* *Stop:* Having a narrow view of success.
* *Start:* Actively listening to others.

*Challenger Safety*

* *Stop:* Ignoring that others influence my emotional state.
* *Start:* Pinpointing people and stressful situations so that they come as less of a surprise.

*Inclusion Safety*

* *Stop:* Stop disregarding the impact my behaviour has upon others.
* *Start:* Asking others for feedback about my behaviour.

Thanks for the tweaks in the 1st paragraph. 

Below, I’ll try to show what kind of difference we see between those 2 penalties:

* The scenario 2.2.3 will apply when the picker will inform us/Agency in advance that he won’t be able to perform the activities in the planned shift due to sick leave/unexpected holidays/holidays. In such a case the agency will have 1 day to find a replacement without being fined. Prior notice is the most important factor here. Real life example - Picker was planned for 6 days, 8 hours each day. On tuesday he informs us that he’s got sick leave from wednesday. In such a case, Agency will have 1 day to find a replacement for other days, if they fail we will provide the replacement but agency’ll be fined (amount of the fine is marginal just to compensate the salary for stand-in)
* Second scenario will apply when Picker won’t show up on the planned shift without prior notice. Real life example - Picker was planned for a shift from 8 AM and he didn’t come. We are trying to call him but he’s not picking up the phone. We are often facing that kind of problem due to the fact that pickers don’t have any responsibility for it, nor the Agency. Mostly, pickers are doing this when they don’t want to work for us any more. 

The idea of the 2nd clause was to:

* Define that we have 1 hour to inform the Agency of such an event (we don’t want to put any fine or any responsibility on us, if we fail; the agency either)
* Define that agency has 2 hours, counted after hour on which we had informed them, to find the replacement without being fined
* Fine them in the amount of 200 PLN for each hour, if they won’t ensure the replacement in given time

We have calendar days - this is why 7/5 conversion is used for keeping the accounts straight. The conversion only solves half of the issue as we still have the operational question: if a person takes a free day, they should have 1 day less in the bank and they receive 5/7 of the pay for it. *_§ 2. Basis for calculating average earnings_*
_(1) The average earnings shall be calculated by taking into account the amounts earned as remuneration. If the amount of remuneration earned in the six months preceding the month in which the calculation is required becomes payable to the staff member after the date of payment of the remuneration calculated on the basis of the average or fixed remuneration, the average remuneration previously paid shall not be recalculated._
_(2) The average remuneration shall be calculated on the basis of the remuneration earned by the employee during the six calendar months preceding the month in which the need for calculation arises and which has become payable to the employee. The month in which the calculation becomes necessary shall be the month in which the event giving rise to the calculation began. For the purpose of calculating holiday pay, the month in which the calculation is due shall be the month in which the penultimate working day before the start of the holiday falls._
_(3) Where a worker has been employed by an employer for less than six calendar months, the calculation of the average remuneration shall be based on the calendar months in respect of which the worker's remuneration became payable. If the need to calculate the average remuneration arises before the first pay day, the average remuneration shall not be calculated and the agreed remuneration shall be paid to the staff member._

*_§ 4. Calculation of the average remuneration for the payment of a calendar day's pay._*
_(1) Average calendar pay shall be calculated, in particular, for the purposes of the payment of sick pay and holiday pay per calendar day paid by the employer._
_(2) For the purpose of calculating the average remuneration for the payment of basic holiday pay and for the payment of additional leave pay provided for in the civil service, national holidays and public holidays shall not be counted as calendar days._
_(3) For the purpose of calculating the average calendar-day remuneration, the remuneration for the period referred to in subsections 2 or 3 of section 2 shall be added together and divided by the number of calendar days in the same period. The number of calendar days on the basis of which the calculation is based shall be reduced by the number of calendar days on which the employee was not paid in the event of refusal to work pursuant to § 19 of the "Employment Contracts Act"._
_(4) For the purpose of calculating average calendar pay in the cases referred to in subsections (4), (5) or (6) of section 2, the remuneration shall be divided by the number of calendar days in the month in which the need for calculation of average remuneration arose._
_(5) In calculating the remuneration payable on the basis of the average calendar days' remuneration, the average calendar days' remuneration shall be multiplied by the number of calendar days for which remuneration is payable._
_(6) If the holiday pay calculated on the basis of the average remuneration for the holiday is less than the remuneration which the staff member would receive if he performed his duties during the same period, the agreed remuneration may be paid to the staff member as holiday pay._

Here is a more generic query for an arbitrary period, taking into account timezones for the selection window as well:

{noformat}SELECT driver_id, car_id, reg_number, CONVERT_TZ(start, 'UTC', 'Europe/London') AS start_london_tz, CONVERT_TZ(end, 'UTC', 'Europe/London') AS end_london_tz
FROM (
    SELECT
        /*+ MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(1000) */
        dsc.driver_id, dsc.car_id, c.reg_number, dsc.start, dsc.end
        FROM taxify_fleet.driver_selected_car dsc
        JOIN taxify_fleet.car c ON c.id = dsc.car_id
        WHERE dsc.end IS NULL
        AND dsc.start <= CONVERT_TZ('2022-08-21 23:59:59', 'Europe/London', 'UTC')
        AND dsc.driver_id IN (123)
    
    UNION

    SELECT
        /*+ MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(1000) */
        dsc.driver_id, dsc.car_id, c.reg_number, dsc.start, dsc.end
        FROM taxify_fleet.driver_selected_car dsc
        JOIN taxify_fleet.car c ON c.id = dsc.car_id
        WHERE dsc.end >= CONVERT_TZ('2022-08-15 00:00:00', 'Europe/London', 'UTC')
        AND dsc.start <= CONVERT_TZ('2022-08-21 23:59:59', 'Europe/London', 'UTC')
        AND dsc.driver_id IN (123)
) selected_cars
ORDER BY driver_id ASC, -end DESC;{noformat}

Thank you for the call today. The situation became much clearer. As discussed during the call, here are the key takeaways:

# If we change the working conditions for the benefit of the employees, it is okay, and we face no risks. If the working conditions change for the worse and it is one-sided change, this can rise risks (mostly termination of employment, compensations, and reputation damage).
# We must follow the principles set out by the law for calculating the remuneration for the leave. That means all the payouts made to the employees that can be considered a wage payment (night-time, over-time, public holiday, bonuses etc.) are included in the calculation. Tax-free payouts (per diem, car compensation) shall not be included.
# As discussed during the call, this can bring attention to the principles of leave calculation, and we have some risk of disparity between what is and what should be. Some employees can come and ask us to remunerate the difference – should they come, we should pay the difference.
# The regulation gives us the possibility to maintain the agreed pay if the average is lower than the agreed pay. This is something that should be decided on the management level, as this is part of employer branding. Most of the companies in Estonia have implemented the principle of keeping the agreed pay if the average is lower. In this situation, I’d recommend following the same principle.
# We will have the conversion issue of calendar days to workdays – this should be evaluated on the operational level. If we see that many employees do not poke this question, we can continue doing business as we have done to this day. The idea is that the employee will not lose any money and the single leave days are not something guaranteed by the law. My recommendation – if there are single cases where this issue is brought up, to solve them ad hoc, otherwise continue the current practice.
# Communication is important\! Even if our Rules of work organization ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/1677426820/Rules+of+Work+Organisation+Estonia)|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/1677426820/Rules+of+Work+Organisation+Estonia)|smart-link]  do not specify the details on how we are calculating (it is stated that we follow the law), we should communicate any changes to the employees. There is a risk that employees could claim the difference between the actual payout and legal payout – the claim can be presented within 3 years. It should be decided how (or if) this is communicated – transparency is good.
# Regarding the question of scheduled employees – as their schedule is not affected by the weekends, their leave should be calculated in accordance with the applicable legislation. If there is an issue with the current set-up, we can take a closer look, but we should know where the main issues are.

What was did:

Added metrics to calculate track locations improvements:

Standart deviations in metrics were calculated in a specific way, the average of values defined previously and mean a max parameter which we expect. For example for speed is 200 km/h, accuracy = 40 meters, time difference = 3 sec (we expect location at least each 3 second). After it we calculate standard deviation by standard formula = sum(power on 2 of (current value - avarage))/count_of_values. And to understand received values more we made sqrt of result. So the result of calculations is a kind of average deviation from the expected value.

{{var locationsCount: Int}} - count of locations which was received in app during the order live
{{var speedStandartDeviation: Double}} - The distance was calculated between every two locations which were received during the order. Then it was converted to km and time between locations was converted to hours. After it distance(km) was divided to time between locations(hours) and we know the speed between each location. After it we can calculate standard deviation.
{{var receivedExpectedRatio: Double}} - We know how many locations we expect by expecting it at least every 2 seconds during the order lifetime. Then we divide the received location count to the expected locations count and convert it to %.
{{var locTimestampStandartDeviation: Double}} - time difference between orders standard deviation
{{var locationsAccuracyStandartDeviation: Double}} - each location accuracy standard deviation
{{var backgroundStatePart: Double}} - how many locations were reported in background in %
{{var foregroundStatePart: Double}} - how many locations were reported in foreground in %
{{var lightweightFlowStatePart: Double}} - how many locations were reported in lightweight in %
